title: Open WebUI signin -- T1087 bcrypt-only-on-match timing reveals registered email addresses
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59218 (GHSA-7rw5-9f7q-xj36,
CVSS 5.3 MEDIUM), affecting Open WebUI prior to 0.10.0.

`/api/v1/auths/signin` looks up a submitted email, and only runs
bcrypt password verification when a matching credential record
EXISTS. Because bcrypt is deliberately slow (that is the point of
using it) and a missing-email response returns immediately without
ever calling it, registered-account signin attempts take measurably
longer than attempts against an email that was never registered --
a classic timing side-channel that lets an unauthenticated caller
enumerate valid account emails purely from response latency, with no
password guessing required.

Detection logic flags a burst of `/api/v1/auths/signin` requests from
a single source targeting many distinct email addresses in a short
window -- the access pattern an automated timing-based enumeration
script produces, distinct from an individual user's occasional
login-failure retries.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact fix commit and PR), fixed in 0.10.0
(runs a dummy bcrypt verification even on a missing email, so timing
no longer distinguishes the two cases).
